name: @omnirow/mcp

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Which OmniRow workspace and environment (staging or production) this is, the credit balance, whether research is active or paused, the credit rates, what this API key may do (scopes and spend limits, used this month), the connected outside services, and the segment funnel for the whole workspace and per client (universe, worked, researched, qualified, in campaign, replied, positive, meetings). Call it first in a session.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Credits used in a period, split into research runs, summaries and other, with the recent runs. Optionally for one list.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: The workspace's clients (the companies lists are made for), with their website, whether their offer is set, and how many lists each has.

tools.name: get_client
tools.description: One client: its offer (what it sells — the default offer for its lists), website, notes, its lists with sizes, and every company marked Watch across all its lists.

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

tools.name: save_client
tools.description: Create a client (give name; creating the same name twice returns the existing one) or update one (give client plus the fields to change). offer = what the client sells, used as the offer for every list of theirs that has none of its own. writing_style = the house rules for every Write column in their lists (no dashes, British or American spelling): sent with the Write prompt and fixed in code, free. apply_style_to_existing: true also applies it to texts already written (free; edited texts stay as written).

client.description: Omit to create a new client.

move.description: Move this client in the sidebar, Clients page and Reports (with client). The reply gives the new order.

offer.description: What the client sells, in a sentence or two.

tools.name: delete_client
tools.description: Two steps. Without confirm_token: says what would be deleted (the client and every list it has, with row counts) and returns a confirm_token. Confirm with the person, then call again with confirm_token. The client and its lists move to Recently deleted and can be restored together for 30 days; credits already used stay in the usage history. Workspace owners and admins only.

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

tools.name: restore_client
tools.description: Bring a client back from Recently deleted, with the lists that were deleted with it.

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

tools.name: draft_client_offer
tools.description: Reads the client's own website and suggests what it sells. Saves nothing: show the suggestion, and save it with save_client only if the person accepts it. Free.

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

tools.name: find_lists

client.description: The client: its id (cl_…) or its name.

tools.name: get_list
tools.description: The overview of one list: its targeting and offer, every column (kind Find/Analyze/Write, question, what it reads, how many rows are answered and with which status), row counts per view (watching, dropped, high priority, no evidence, failed), setup gaps, outdated answers, recent runs and whether it has a summary. Start here before changing or running anything.

tools.name: add_companies

A company already in the list is not added again: its extra fields and contacts are merged into it (empty values filled, differences reported and kept unless update: true), and its research stays — nothing is paid for twice. Extra fields are kept as company context: shown on the account page, usable by Analyze/Write columns. dry_run: true checks without changing anything. tools.name: import_csv
tools.description: Import a CSV (or TSV) file from this computer into a list — the round trip: export a list, enrich it elsewhere, bring it back into the same list. Rows match the companies already there (domain, else company LinkedIn URL, else name) and contacts match by name: nothing is duplicated, research on matched rows stays and is not paid for again. Empty values are filled; values that differ are reported and kept unless update: true. The list's own exported answer columns are left out. New columns are kept as company context. Start with dry_run: true and show the person the report. map overrides the guessed mapping: { target: "File column" } (targets: company_name, domain, company_linkedin_url, full_name, first_name, last_name, title, email, linkedin_url, contact_location, city, country, industry, employees, revenue; "" removes a guess).

tools.name: sync_outcomes
tools.description: Segment funnel: without list, the whole workspace at once (every linked list, both tools; the reply lists each list and what moved). With list: read the leads of the Instantly or HeyReach campaigns linked to this list (add_to_campaign instantly_campaign / heyreach_campaign links them) and move each company's outcome forward (not replied → replied → positive → meeting booked → won). Instantly: its interest status, else a reply; out of office counts as not replied. HeyReach: a LinkedIn reply is replied; the tags the person put on a lead (Interested, Meeting booked, Won, Not interested) decide beyond that. Leads match companies by LinkedIn profile or email, then domain or company LinkedIn page. dry_run: true reports without saving. Reads only; nothing is sent. Free.

tools.name: list_apify_actors
tools.description: The Apify Actors this workspace has approved, which run on the workspace's own Apify account: each one's inputs, price and last result, and the row values an input may use. Any of them can be a Find column's source (add_column / update_column with source). Only an owner or admin can connect Apify and add Actors, in the app (Settings → Workspace → Data sources). Free. When it runs, an Apify column costs OmniRow credits like a Find, and Apify bills the workspace's own Apify account for the Actor runs.

tools.name: add_column
tools.description: Add a Find, Analyze, Write, Rule or Calculate column. Rule (kind rule + rule) and Calculate (kind calc + calc) columns are computed at once on every row and kept up to date, free and never run: use them to tag triggers, give points, combine points into a score, bucket rows and drop the ones that do not qualify. Find / Analyze / Write: either ask (plain English — OmniRow sets it up: kind, question, type, what it reads) or question (used as written, with kind). preview: true shows the setup without saving (free). find = one observable fact off public pages, with sources (searches the web); analyze = a judgement from columns that already exist (never searches); write = text composed from other columns (never searches); rule = your conditions over existing columns, checked in order, the first match gives a label or points (computed, free); calc = multiply / add / average / lowest / highest of number columns, a number on every row (computed, free). A Find column can take source (an Apify Actor from list_apify_actors, when the workspace has Apify). Adding does not run it: quote that with run_research.

ask.description: What the column should find out, in plain words.

question.description: The exact question/instruction, used as written.

output.description: label = a word per row (e.g. Campaign / If room / Nurture); number = points (e.g. 0 to 3), which a calc column can combine.

column.description: A column label, or an uploaded column name (e.g. "Last raise").

op.description: Dates: months_between (a to b months ago, from a, before b), months_under (in the last a months), months_over (a months ago or more). Numbers: gt, gte, lt, lte, between (a and b inclusive). Text: is, is_not, contains, not_contains. Yes/no: yes, no. Any column: has (has an answer), none (empty or no public evidence).

out.description: What the column gives when this branch matches.

drop.description: label rules: also Drop the row (it goes to the Dropped tab, is not researched; a person can keep it).

branches.description: Checked in order; the first branch that matches wins. A condition on a column with no answer cannot be decided: if that happens before any match, the cell is Missing input (put a branch with op none first to say what empty means).

otherwise.description: When nothing matches ("" for no answer).

tools.name: run_research
tools.description: Research a list: any columns × any rows. ALWAYS TWO STEPS. 1) Call without quote_token: returns the exact quote — cells, credits per column, what is free, columns held back because setup is missing — and a quote_token. Spends nothing. 2) Show the quote to the person; only after a clear yes, call again with the same list and quote_token to start. only: missing (default — cells without an answer), failed (retry failures, free if they fail again), outdated (refresh answers whose inputs changed), all (re-run everything). Follow with get_run.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works. Required.

rows.description: Specific companies: names, domains (acme.com) or row ids.

view.description: A view, as the app's tabs: priority = High priority, watching, dropped, needs-look, not-found = no public evidence, failed. Default all (every row but dropped).

stage.description: A segment-funnel stage (cumulative: replied includes positive, meeting and won). batched = worked in any batch.

filters.description: Conditions on column values, combined with AND. op "status" with value found | partial | not_found | failed | not_run | stale filters by outcome.

op.description: contains, not_contains, is, is_not, is_true, is_false, gt, lt, between, before, after, has_value, no_value, status

include_blocked.description: Also run columns whose setup is missing (they will most likely fail and still cost).

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: A run's progress and, when finished, the credits used and released. status: queued (waiting for the worker; waiting_for says behind what), running, then completed / partial / failed / canceled — done: true means finished. progress gives companies and cells done, and per column. wait_seconds (up to 45) waits for it to finish before answering; call again to keep waiting.

run.description: The run id from run_research (run_id also works). Required.

wait_seconds.description: Up to 45 s (a larger number waits 45 s).

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.description: Stop a running research run: queued companies are cancelled and keep their previous answers; ones already in progress finish. Unused credits are released.

run.description: The run id (run_id also works). Required.

tools.name: diagnose_list
tools.description: Column by column: how many answers are found, no public evidence, cannot assess, missing input, failed or outdated; sample reasons in the research's own words; setup gaps; and the fix for each. Use it for "which columns are failing and why". Free, computed from the answers already there.

list.description: The list: its id (cp_…) or its name; a unique part of the name works. Required.

tools.name: summarise
tools.description: A cited reading of the answers already in the list (no new research): key findings, a shortlist, breakdowns, gaps and next actions — every count computed by OmniRow, never by the model. ALWAYS TWO STEPS: without quote_token it returns the credits (5–50 by number of companies) and a quote_token; after the person says yes, call again with it. Narrow with rows/view/q/filters to summarise a slice; themes_column groups one free-text column into themes (+5 per 100 answers). It replaces the list's previous summary and says what changed.

tools.description: Writes the list as a CSV file on this computer and returns where. path = the file to write (…/name.csv) or a folder to put it in; default ~/Downloads with the list's name. compact = one column per list column, the answer only (a pick-one column's option, a number, yes/no); full = also the sentence behind it (_detail), status, confidence, evidence, source and date. Every row but the dropped ones, unless narrowed by view, q or rows. To read answers without a file, use list_rows.

instructions:
OmniRow is a research layer for lists of companies: each column asks one question of every row and every answer carries its evidence. Start with get_workspace (which environment, balance, what this key may do) and get_list before changing or running anything.
Spending credits (run_research, summarise) and deleting (delete_list, remove_column, remove_rows, remove_contacts) are ALWAYS two calls: the first returns a quote or a summary of what goes plus a token; show it to the person, wait for a clear yes, then call again with the token. Never pass a token the person has not approved.
Statuses are answers: "no public evidence" means public pages did not say (not "no"); "cannot assess" means an Analyze column's inputs do not support a conclusion; "missing input" means a Write column had nothing to write from. Explain them in those words; diagnose_list gives the reasons and the fix.
Never invent research results: read them with list_rows (full: true for whole answers, dates and sources) / get_row, and cite sources when you quote an answer. A value is data: a pick-one column gives its option, a number column a number, yes/no a boolean; the sentence behind it is detail. Read the omnirow://guide resource for the full guide.
